Today's meeting of the National Assembly commenced at 1:24 PM under the chairmanship of the Right Honourable Chairperson Mr. Narayan Prasad Dahal.
Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable members,
(1:24 PM)
Names have been received to speak. The proceedings will now commence. Honourable members, I will provide time for Honourable members to speak during the Zero Hour.
First, Honourable Member Kamala Pant.
Honourable Mr. Kamala Pant (Nepali Congress):- Right Honourable Chairperson,
(1:24 PM)
Last year in Bhadra, on Bhadra 23 and 24, it was said. And on the 23rd, a movement occurred. A commission called the Gauri Commission, led by Gauri Bahadur Karki, was formed regarding the incident that happened during the movement. The commission submitted its report. However, the report submitted by that investigation commission has not been made public by the government yet. Now, regarding the incident of the 24th, the Nepali people are demanding that a judicial investigation commission be formed, an investigation be conducted, and the truth be revealed. So many incidents have occurred, so many movements, and this Gengji movement on the 24th was the most destructive incident of the past year, the incident of Bhadra 24th last year. An investigation commission has not yet been formed for that incident; let it be formed and investigated. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Jayanti Devi Rai.
(1:25 PM)
Honourable Mr. Jayanti Devi Rai (Communist Party of Nepal):-
(1:26 PM)
Right Honourable Chairperson, sports are an attraction for youth. It is also a pride of Nepal that introduces us to the international arena. However, Nepali players are unable to participate in the X-port games to be held from October 3 to 18 due to financial constraints. The Sports Council is not paying attention to these sports. Therefore, there is also a dispute regarding these e-Xport games. I would like to draw the government's attention to this and request that a single official mechanism be created and that youth and players not be deprived of international sports. They have won medals repeatedly and have the opportunity to win again, so I draw your attention to this.
Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Tul Prasad Bishwakarma.
(1:27 PM)
Honourable Mr. Tul Prasad Bishwakarma (Rastriya Janamorcha):- Right Honourable Chairperson,
(1:27 PM)
Recently, the situation where landless squatters have been evicted and housed in various camps has led to a sharp increase in suicides among them, with 11 people having died so far, including the latest incident. In the latest incident, Chamar Bahadur Nepali was displaced from the Gairigaun settlement, and he used to work in a brick kiln. His body was found hanging from a tree near the brick kiln just two days ago. Similarly, Hiralal Hazar Dusad, 47 years old, was at the agricultural training center in Bode, and he was found hanging in his room. I want to ask the government, why are landless squatters being... (Time expired).
Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Narayan Dutt Mishra.
(1:28 PM)
Honourable Mr. Narayan Dutt Mishra (Nepali Congress):- Right Honourable Chairperson,
(1:28 PM)
Far-Western Nepal has its own suffering. In settlements 700 kilometers away from the capital, just as the sunrise is late and the monsoon arrives late, the government's pace of development is also slow. Hydropower projects in Seti, Karnali, Mahakali, and Budhiganga have been left incomplete. Furthermore, Far-Western Nepal is struggling with basic problems such as roads, health, education, employment, and drinking water. During the rainy season, there is the threat of landslides and floods; in winter, they are forced to go to India for work. If they get a big job, they make a living as watchmen. Similarly, their needs are blacktopping of roads, treatment in hospitals, employment for youth, and fertilizer and irrigation for farmers, they say. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Bhuvan Bahadur Sunar.
(1:29 PM)
Honourable Mr. Bhuvan Bahadur Sunar (Communist Party of Nepal):- Right Honourable Chairperson,
(1:29 PM)
Sir, the two-day government holiday has become impractical. Due to the Saturday and Sunday holiday, the public is unable to receive services in hospitals, and the situation is chaotic. Similarly, schools are also in a state of disarray. Therefore, I demand that this two-day holiday be immediately abolished. Also, there are six days of holiday for festivals, from Phulpati to Dashami, but since the Rana era until today, there are 15 days of holiday in the courts from Ghatasthapana to Purnima. Therefore, I strongly demand that this be reduced to six days. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Madan Kumari Shah "Garima".
(1:30 PM)
Honourable Mr. Madan Kumari Shah "Garima" (Communist Party of Nepal):- Right Honourable Chairperson,
(1:30 PM)
Sir, there is a word 'bachkana', which is a Hindi word. It means that a person's behavior, speech, or decisions are not mature according to their age and responsibility. And due to such childish decisions of this government, 11 people who were staying in holding centers, who were forcibly displaced, have died so far. Recently, Chamar Bahadur Nepali, aged 50, and Hiralal Hajara Dusad, aged 47, have died. They chose suicide. Why do people commit suicide? People commit suicide when they have no other option left. I want to ask this government, through you, Mr. Chairperson, what kind of development are you seeking by killing the poor? I demand, through you, Mr. Chairperson, permanent settlement for those in the holding centers. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Yuvraj Sharma.
(1:39 PM)
Honourable Mr. Yuvraj Sharma (Nepali Congress):- Right Honourable Chairperson, today
(1:32 PM)
Nepalis are concerned about the rising graph of tuberculosis, Japanese encephalitis, and malaria. Meanwhile, the landslide victims in Jajarkot are facing serious problems due to colds and fevers in the camps. Instead of paying attention to these issues, some Honourable Ministers are seen threatening voters to secure their votes, while some ruling party MPs are seen disrespecting the Honourable Speaker's call and leaving the meeting in a huff. Right Honourable Chairperson, a major reason for the current inflation and scarcity in the market is the government's weak monitoring and lack of attention to the distribution system. Similarly, the increasing deficit in electricity trade is also a result of the government's incompetent policies. Through you, Right Honourable Chairperson, I want to draw the government's attention towards the solution of all these problems. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Rajendra Laxmi Gaire.
(1:32 PM)
Honourable Mr. Rajendra Laxmi Gaire (Communist Party of Nepal):- Right Honourable Chairperson,
(1:33 PM)
Sir, due to the incessant rainfall on Bhadra 3, 2083, 19 houses in Hostigaun, Ward No. 10 of Rampur Municipality, have been damaged. It is heard that this monsoon will last for another month and a half. I want to draw the attention of the government and all concerned bodies to this. I am saddened to hear about the deaths of 19 people from landless settlements. Why are people dying in places secured for safety from the Bagmati River floods? Are they being taken to be killed or to be saved? I demand an answer from the government. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Suresh Kumar Ale Magar.
(1:33 PM)
Honourable Mr. Suresh Kumar Ale Magar (Communist Party of Nepal):- Right Honourable Chairperson,
(1:34 PM)
Sir, religion and state are very important and serious matters. So, what can be said in one minute? However, as there is a prevailing sentiment for a religious state at this time, I would like to briefly state a few things. Religion is purely a personal matter; no institution, body, or country has a religion, nor should it. For example, what is the religion of the National Assembly? It has no religion, nor should it. The Chairperson of the National Assembly, we members, and the staff may have their own religions, but similarly, Nepal does not have a religion; its citizens have religions. A religious state certainly exists where there is a monarchy. In a dictatorial Panchayat system, there was a religious state, but in a democratic country, in a democratic system, such a religious state does not and should not exist. Therefore, I want to draw everyone's attention to this matter. Personal freedom, religious freedom is a personal affair, not a state affair, not a national affair. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable members, the order of speaking during the Zero Hour concludes here.
(1:35 PM)
Honourable members, names have been received on a party basis for speaking during the Special Time. I will now provide time for the Honourable members to speak. First, Honourable Member Lalit Jung Shahi, time 18 minutes. Following this, Honourable Member Nar Bahadur Bista.
Honourable Mr. Lalit Jung Shahi (Nepali Congress):- Right Honourable Chairperson,
(1:35 PM)
In this Special Time today, I intend to raise some issues of national concern and public concern with the time allocated to me. The first issue I wish to raise in my Special Time today is the establishment of an international humanitarian organization in Nepal, the Red Cross. I would like to recall that the Nepal Red Cross Society was established in Nepal on Bhadra 19, 2020 BS, when the then His Majesty's Government of Nepal signed the Geneva Convention related to International Humanitarian Law. In its initial days, the Nepal Red Cross Society distributed blankets to the victims, disaster victims, and the sick, took them to hospitals on stretchers, and then started ambulance services. In later days, with the permission of the Government of Nepal and a Council of Ministers' decision, the Nepal Red Cross Society took responsibility for blood donation for life, blood transfusion services, and blood donation services throughout Nepal. To this day, the Nepal Red Cross Society has been saving the lives of millions of Nepalis through its blood donation services.
Not only by saving lives, but the Nepal Red Cross Society has also appealed for assistance from various international donor agencies and has provided community health services, eye treatment services, and safe drinking water facilities for the extremely poor and destitute people in the remote hilly and mountainous regions, as well as in the Terai region. In the context of providing relief and services to the public, the Nepal Red Cross Society, through an agreement with the WFP (World Food Programme), has also provided food for work for the people in remote areas. Despite providing so much relief and service, on July 28, 2020 (2077 BS, Shrawan 12), the then government suddenly suspended the Nepal Red Cross Society, an impartial, independent, and neutral organization that has been serving the Nepali people with a selfless spirit in a neutral and independent manner, suspending its central committee and placing the Nepal Red Cross Society under an ad-hoc arrangement. Today, for the fifth time, the government of various times, including the recent government, has placed the Nepal Red Cross Society under ad-hoc arrangements repeatedly, and the various international donor agencies provide assistance and humanitarian services that the Red Cross has been providing...

They were in a state of stagnation and obstruction. Honorable Chairperson, we are all aware of the 2072 earthquake. The people of the 14 most affected districts and their representatives may recall today that the Nepal Red Cross Society, through its organization, mobilized billions of rupees in aid and provided relief to the earthquake victims. Even when the government did not provide cash, the victims, the earthquake victims, were provided with cash assistance. Not only that, during the time of COVID, how much suffering and pain the people of this country endured. Even during such a pandemic, the Nepal Red Cross Society provided significant assistance, service, and relief to the Nepali people. Now, Chairperson, in the month of Poush, 2082, this organization called the Nepal Red Cross Society, as I mentioned earlier, was established by the government by signing the Geneva Convention. Its preamble states that the Nepal Red Cross Society shall function as a supporting organization of the Government of Nepal. While it has been providing significant assistance and support that the government should provide to the people, it has been brought under ad-hoc management. Its parent organizations are the International Federation of Red Cross (IFRC). Its further parent organization is the International Committee of Red Cross (ICRC). With their support and coordination, collecting suggestions and advice from the district level, the General Convention held in Chitwan on the 24th and 25th of Poush, 2082, formulated a new statute for the Nepal Red Cross Society. This statute was certified by the Chief District Officer of Kathmandu on the 23rd of Magh, 2082, instructing to proceed with the Nepal Red Cross Society according to this new amended statute. As per the directions of that statute, elections were held from the district level to the central level, and the election schedule was issued. Accordingly, the election process began in the month of Baishakh, and the election of the central committee was completed on the 24th of Asar. While the election process was moving forward according to the statute that it itself had certified and approved, the same Chief District Officer who had certified it, on the 21st of Baishakh, 2083, after the election process had begun as per the statute, used the authority granted by the statute to issue a directive to obstruct the election of the Nepal Red Cross Society, thereby halting the election process. Currently, the Red Cross is in a state of stagnation. As I mentioned earlier, the Red Cross organization is unable to provide services and facilities to the people due to various services and facilities that the Nepali people have been deprived of. This has caused great loss to the Nepali people. I request the relevant ministry, the Ministry of Women, Children and Senior Citizens, and the Ministry of Home Affairs, to free the Red Cross from ad-hocism, to allow the Red Cross to conduct its activities in accordance with the values and principles of the International Red Cross and the laws of Nepal, and to open the way for the completion of the suspended elections. My second issue, Honorable Chairperson, is that various commissions are formed in Nepal. Constitutional commissions are constitutional commissions, but the government also forms various commissions based on necessity. A commission was formed in 2076 under the chairmanship of Mohan Raman Bhattarai, former chairman of the Special Court, to ascertain the facts about the land encroached upon and illegally occupied by various individuals and land mafias, including government, public, and Guthi lands, and to submit a report to the government. That commission has submitted its report. The report states that 8,192 ropanis of land in various parts of the country are under encroachment and have been illegally occupied. The report was submitted to the government asking it to reclaim and return these lands. It has been many days since this report was submitted. While only a nominal amount of land has been returned, it has been 7 years since 2076 to 2083. The previous governments have not taken action, and the current government has also not paid attention to this issue. I urge the government to reclaim all these government, public, and Guthi lands. I urge the government to act with urgency in this matter. I request this government to do what previous governments did not want to do, could not do, or failed to do, and to provide a sense of good governance. Chairperson, my third issue is happiness. Let none of us be mistaken; happiness is not just news. Chairperson, there is a tradition of celebrating various international days, such as Women's Day, Labor Day, etc. There is one day celebrated in the world, and that day is International Day of Happiness. The UN General Assembly decided in 2012 to celebrate International Day of Happiness. In a survey conducted in 2025 to determine which country's citizens are happy and which country's citizens are happy, based on various criteria, Finland was certified as the happiest country with the happiest people. Denmark is second, Iceland is third, Sweden is fourth, Netherlands is fifth, and Costa Rica is among the countries with happy people who have achieved happiness. These countries are listed as the happiest countries in the world. This proves that happiness is not just about increasing wealth and money. Because the richest and most prosperous country in the world, America, ranks 23rd in happiness, and the United Kingdom ranks 24th in happiness. This year, March 20th, International Day of Happiness, is celebrated on March 20th. Chairperson, the criteria for this are: the GDP growth rate of the country, the per capita income, the life expectancy, how healthy the people are, whether there is quality education, and how much access the citizens have to the rights and facilities guaranteed by the constitution and human-like services. Based on these, the evaluation is done, and then it is called a country of happy people. It is said with sadness, when will Nepal move in that direction? My best wishes to the current government, the majority government of Prachanda, that this government may function as a stable government for 5 years and succeed in making Nepal known as a country with happy people who have achieved happiness. I urge and draw the attention of the new government, the current communist government with a majority of Prachanda, that in the coming years, the policies, programs, and budget formulation of this government should succeed in registering Nepal among the nations that celebrate International Day of Happiness as a nation with happy people. Finally, we form these commissions. Just recently, in a meeting of one of our committees, the Honorable Chairperson of the National Human Rights Commission and the Secretaries came and presented their report, clarifying the state of human rights. They have their own grievances. They stated that based on the complaints received and the investigations and evaluations conducted for human rights, they recommend to the government that human rights have been violated and infringed upon, and that action should be taken. However, the government remains silent and does not respond positively. Similarly, various other commissions are formed. I mentioned earlier that the report submitted by the commission formed under the chairmanship of Mohan Raman Bhattarai regarding the encroachment of Guthi, public, and government lands has not been implemented to date. Why are these commissions formed? Why are the reports of the commissions not implemented? The government should pay attention to these matters. And the commission formed under the chairmanship of Gauri Bahadur Karki on August 23rd, regarding the events of the 23rd and 24th, submitted a report, which I consider partial, not complete, on the events of the 23rd. This report has not been made public to date. The government should implement the demands and contents of that report. My question is, should Gauri Bahadur Karki be allowed to keep the allowances and facilities he received, or should they be recovered? Because he was asked to investigate and report on the events of the 23rd and 24th. The events of the 24th, that act of terrorism, unprecedented in Nepal, not even occurring during the 10-year conflict, the Supreme Court, Parliament, Singha Durbar, and the damage to various individuals and commercial establishments, which are against the spirit and intention of the system established by the constitution of this country, were not seen by Gauri Bahadur Karki's commission. Therefore, I express my regret towards Gauri Bahadur Karki for remaining silent without investigating and reporting on the events of the 24th. I demand from the government that all the facilities received by Gauri Bahadur Karki be recovered. Thank you. Jai Nepal. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Nar Bahadur Bista, time 13 minutes. (13:53) After this, Honorable Member Somnath Poudel. Honorable Mr. Nar Bahadur Bista (Nepal Communist Party): Honorable Chairperson (13:54) Sir, I am going to speak on some contemporary issues. The Bheri Lift Drinking Water Project, which was initiated in Surkhet, the capital of Karnali Province, during the tenure of the then Honorable Prime Minister Prachanda in 2081-82 with the support of the World Bank, has been awarded to a contractor. Today, that contract has been terminated by the current IT-friendly government. There is a severe water crisis in Surkhet, the capital of Karnali. We have received information that a project with approximately 25% completion has been canceled. What I want to say in this regard is that with the support of the World Bank and the Asian Development Bank, Nepal's public procurement system laws, the Public Procurement Act, 2063, the establishment of the Public Procurement Monitoring Office, the legal provisions of the Review Commission, and various systems such as procurement system bidding, and government have been initiated. As a result, collusion among contractors, the end of brokerage practices, and the control of goondaism were also included. Previously, only a few contractors could participate by submitting high bids. Considering this, the then government introduced an e-bidding system. This led to the end of collusion among contractors and the development of a competitive system. Recently, some individuals were prosecuted on charges of unauthorized access to the bidding system, manipulation of bids, and tampering with bids. For example, individuals from Kalika Construction Builders were apprehended. Due to these reasons, what has happened is that the procurement system and bidding processes initiated with the support of the World Bank and the Asian Development Bank have been terminated, and contracts initiated with the investment of donor agencies, such as the Bheri Lift...

I said, drinking water projects, Kathmandu Valley Drinking Water Project's 5 packages, have been cancelled one after another with various contractors and new tenders are being called in a way that the system will be handed over to ADB and World Bank funded road projects. This notice has come. The e-government system that the government has, its source code is with an Indian company. Where is its code? It's with some Indian company. But that contractor directs that if this person and that person colluded and took it, then the current Jengji government has cancelled dozens of such contracts by submitting hard copies. This is objectionable. They call themselves IT, we started IT. When Krishna Bahadur Mahara was the minister, this internet service started with the slogan 'Internet in every house, mobile in every hand'. Those who are now coming in the name of IT and agitating, this is not the government of friends who have come to power in the name of IT, but today they are cancelling those IT procurement processes, submitting hard copies, and in a gangster style, for their own projects, those who are called 35 years old, a minister who is not even 30 years old comes, here in the front of the house, while answering the honorable member's questions, starts from 35 years, who doesn't even know the history of 35 years. When was he born, what did I do, living in Kathmandu, eating the property of his parents, and becoming honorable and a minister, these friends say here, what did you do for 35 years? I will also provide the data for that. What was not done in 35 years, what happened. But who gave you the authority to cancel the contract for the work done in 35 years? Who gave you the authority to settle the contract by submitting a hard copy? And you say you are going to the age of IT, therefore, the drinking water project of Chaunveni Lift has been cancelled, and Melamchi is being pushed back by 20-30 years, and the same is happening to the capital of Karnali Province, there should be an immediate investigation. Because just recently, the Minister of Physical Infrastructure visited the capital of Karnali Province. After coming back, he got the contract cancelled. Is this collusion or what? Therefore, what I want to call for is that the source code which is in India, is with some company in India, at least make that source code in Nepal and keep it in Nepal. Let the Nepalis run it. And then investigate whether there was collusion or not. I want to call for that. On the other hand, there is a kind of panic right now, that experienced employees, according to the 2049 Act, Rule 36(6) of 2050, due to the age limit, those who have 1 year left to retire, will not be transferred, this is in the constitution, in the law. But today, joint secretaries are being transferred and so much panic is being caused that citing 30 years and 55 years, those joint secretaries who have worked loyally for the nation until now, who have 9 years left to retire, 4 months to retire, are being transferred and kept in the Ministry of General Administration. Dozens of joint secretaries are kept in the Ministry of Home Affairs as unclaimed. The bureaucracy is being threatened and tired, and the government is trying to run the country from the minister's secretariat, how will this country become? Where are you taking this country? I want to ask the government. You have studied the history of 36 years. Prime Minister for 36 years? Or for bringing the republic in 36 years, a person like me still has bullet fragments in my hands. This republic was brought by being injured by 5 bullets, the freedom to speak in this republic, you have come to power by playing with the freedom brought by the proponents of the republic, the republicans? But you do whatever you want, saying what happened in 35 years. I, the Honorable Chairperson, the roads we have, the four-lane roads, the six-lane roads, you drive them without using the brakes, you are the ones who drive the cars. Electricity production has increased from 600 megawatts to 4200 megawatts. Today I heard a news, what did our Energy Minister say? In response to the question of why the power went out, he said it was the old system, because of the old system, the power went out. Look! The old system produced 4200 megawatts. And the Prime Minister comes and says in the meeting that if you use an induction stove, the transport will be overloaded, so don't use it. Will the country run with such logic? Many such examples of 35 years have been given by honorable members here. I don't need to give many arguments. But to run the country, the way you have, we have seen the entertainment, the festivals, the styles, the behaviors of your House of Representatives. Therefore, what I want to say to you, what I want to suggest is, at least read the constitution. Honorable friends, I want to tell the honorable members of this National Assembly that today their press is running due to yesterday's festival, it's fine. It's natural. But the country cannot run by just abusing 35 years. Your own plans, your own intelligence, thousands of martyrs have sacrificed for the establishment of the nation, nationality, federalism, and republic, thousands of warriors have endured imprisonment and brought freedom, questioning that freedom, and being unable to do anything yourself, abusing others, the country will not be saved, it seems to me. Therefore, what I want to suggest to this government is, at least you are doing new things. The other day, the Minister of Physical Infrastructure, returning from Darchula in Sudurpaschim, came to Baitadi, caught a cold, chartered a helicopter and came to Kathmandu, spent 16 lakhs, that is also new. The other day, the private secretary of the Home Minister, when there was an agitation in Biratnagar, booked a Skyvan and went, spent 8 lakhs. We did not do that in 35 years. Not even 35 years, not even 20 years, we did not do that much in 34 years. You have appointed secretaries at the joint secretary level in your ministry. In the past, our ministers had appointed only three or four private secretaries at the undersecretary level. In the Prime Minister's Office, you have appointed 27 people with facilities equivalent to a minister. We did not do that. No prime minister had appointed advisors with facilities equivalent to a minister. You have done this new thing too. We have done good work in 35 years as well. But in just five months, you have exploited the state many times more than that and are looting the state's property. Today, there is a line at the passport office, a line for gas, a line everywhere. A line to light electricity, and you have done new things? Even during the Indian blockade six months ago, gas was available in one or two hours. Today, that blockade is not in place. So what is the fault? The old ones. To the ministers of 25-30 years, I want to suggest, at least read history. Reading history, saying to parents, 'This is not my parent, it's been 36 years, I don't consider this father my father', is that acceptable? Insulting parents? Will the country be built by insulting parents, by abusing parents? Will the nation be built? Therefore, I want to suggest that at least learn to respect parents, learn to honor parents. On the other hand, the kind of wrong narrative you are creating, the society is going into a quagmire, how to make people civilized socially, politically, morally, can be known from your Facebook walls, the country will not run by abusing people. Therefore, in conclusion, through the Honorable Chairperson, I want to say that at least learn the lessons of civilization and history, read history, and learn how to run the country. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable member Somnath Potal. Time 15 minutes. (14:07 hrs) After this, Honorable member Chandra Bahadur KC. Honorable Shri Somnath Potal (Nepal Communist Party, UML): Honorable Chairperson, I would like to express my heartfelt gratitude for the time. Honorable Chairperson, I had heard a song in a Hindi film, "When the one above gives, he gives abundantly." This time, the election and today's speech felt the same to me. Other times I get to speak for two minutes, three minutes, five minutes, today the Chairperson gave me 15 minutes. Now, when Raswapa said they would do 100 things easily if they got 182 seats, they themselves evaluated that they reached almost an A+ grade, but the public says it's NG, NG, and a bit more, D, they completed 34, 36 percent. Now, if they could determine the time themselves like their evaluation, I would also speak for 15 minutes according to my own calculations, but here the Chairperson will cut the line again. Therefore, I want to set the time according to how much I can speak from the beginning. First of all, there is a tradition in our parliamentary practice that if we have to ask the ministers, the government, we have to do it through the Honorable Chairperson. If, while speaking, due to time constraints, it is not possible to say it through the Honorable Chairperson, then all the questions I have asked will be conveyed through the Honorable Chairperson, I want to inform you of this at the beginning, and I seek permission to present my views. This morning, citizens from Sudurpaschim sent a message to be conveyed to the ministers. What is this message? In their language, it is said, isn't it about Sudurpaschim? "Are the ministers well? If you have a cold, we will send a helicopter with great affection. If the helicopter doesn't come, a Skyvan of the army will come. Don't be afraid, don't worry." This is from Sudurpaschim. Now there is also a message from the Nepali public. Perhaps this is the public's message. You might have asked this question for the first time, the public has asked in the same language. You asked what the Prime Minister ate, what vegetables he ate. Now the public is asking such questions, "Did the minister eat? What did he cook it with? Gas or firewood?" The ministers probably cooked with gas, but the public cannot cook with gas. The situation of the public is such that a little while ago, in the villages, there was a custom of 'mourning feast', today it is a situation where even the mourning feast has to be cut. I don't know about other places, but in our eastern part, there was a custom of 'mourning feast'. There was nothing else in the mourning feast. And if someone died, the custom was to soak rice, then add a little jaggery, and later sugar, and serve the mourning feast. The custom was to eat soaked rice with jaggery. Now, if we light gas, there is no gas, if we light firewood, as was the case the other day, firewood is also not available. Now, if you are living in a rented house in the city, where will you light a fire? If you light an induction stove, it's unaffordable. The line goes on one side, that's always there, the other expense is unaffordable. Therefore, the public's situation is such that they have to cut the day by soaking rice and adding a little sugar. The ministers probably always have gas, they are eating, what are they cooking with? The public has asked to ask the ministers. I also want to ask that on behalf of the public. Then there is another situation, some scientists are saying now...

I've seen it. If you look from the moon, China's Great Wall was visible until recently, but now two things are visible! Nepal has added to that, which is the gas pipeline. The situation where people are lining up for gas is now visible from the moon. I want to ask the honorable ministers when this situation will end. Honorable Chairperson, Parliament is not a place for political revenge or blind opposition. I believe that every word spoken in this supreme representative body of the people must be based on facts, and I would like to urge that what I have stated is also based on facts. Let's discuss the facts. Now, while saying let's discuss the facts, if our honorable ministers speak here after a while, their first question will be 'What happened in 35 years?' 'What did you do in 35 years?' they will ask, unlike people like us from the villages. They ask questions. Now, the ministers are educated. They have 'Doctor' in front of their names. They also mix a little English while speaking, which is why I think, I can guess, they have read a lot. Since they are learned people, I believe that the Ministry of Finance is now through you. On the basis of that trust, honorable ministers, please read the Economic Survey 2083 once before coming here to speak. In the remaining areas, work is underway to provide electricity access through alternative energy sources along with the expansion of the national transmission system. So far, through the Alternative Energy Promotion Center, 6,719 kilowatts of electricity have been generated from 207 micro and small hydropower projects in Karnali, benefiting 64,231 households. Similarly, 1,709 kilowatts of electricity have been generated from 23 solar mini-grids, providing electricity access to 5,395 households. Out of a total of 718 wards in Karnali, 82 wards are fully electrified by the national transmission line, 472 wards are partially electrified, and 164 wards are yet to be reached by the national transmission line. I would like to inform you that the government is moving forward with its future plan, considering this not just as a matter of data but as a responsibility linked to basic services and social justice for the citizens.
Honorable Chairperson, the Ministry of Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation, Nepal Electricity Authority, and Alternative Energy Promotion Center jointly identified 101,187 households and geographical areas in Karnali that were yet to be electrified in 2079 and prepared and implemented the Last Mile Electrification Project. After the government's campaign to electrify these areas, electricity is yet to be provided to approximately 10,000 households in 13 municipalities. Currently, the Nepal Electricity Authority and the Alternative Energy Promotion Center are conducting electrification programs by classifying work areas. We understand that this indicates progress in the electrification of Karnali. I would also like to inform you that significant work is being done on transmission and sub-stations in Karnali Province. The 132 kV Surkhet sub-station has already come into operation. The 32-kilometer-long double-circuit 132 kV Surkhet-Dailekh transmission line is under construction and is targeted for completion by next Asar. Similarly, work is underway to complete the under-construction 132 kV Chuprabazar sub-station in Dailekh by next Poush. The bidding process for the Dailekh, Kalikot, Jumla 132 kV transmission line has moved forward. Various packages for the construction of 33 or 11 kV sub-stations and distribution lines in districts like Kalikot, Jumla, Rukum Paschim, Jajarkot, Salyan, Mugu, and Humla are in implementation. Physical progress in Jumla and Kalikot areas is around 60 percent, and in other districts, it is between 40 to 70 percent. The government is also advancing work in alternative energy in parallel. An 8 MW grid-connected solar power project has been initiated with loan assistance from the Asian Development Bank. Land for this has been selected in Dailekh, Rukum Paschim, and Jumla. Furthermore, budget has been allocated for the construction of solar home systems, small hydropower, and solar mini-grids in remote wards, and programs are being implemented.
Honorable Chairperson, I would also like to state that we have made arrangements to send the budget, which was previously centralized in the ministry, to the provinces and the respective distribution centers in a decentralized manner. And where the people's representatives are active, the work has also been done more quickly. We welcome the Honorable Members representing those areas from our ministry. For this year's program, the ministry is also ready to add more budget to the areas of public interest by coordinating with the relevant distribution centers, irrigation offices, or provincial chiefs. Also, a 30 MW solar project in Dailekh is in the final stages of PPAs; if completed, along with the 132 kV line from Surkhet to Dailekh and the electricity for Jajarkot and Kalikot this year, it will provide great relief to Karnali. The construction of Jagadulla has begun, which has also facilitated road access and transmission line work up to Dolpa. I humbly request the Honorable Members to provide guidance, some cooperation, and coordination for social justice and quality electricity, and these works will be expedited. Many Honorable Members have also come to the ministry and taken programs for their areas, districts, and provinces, and we have addressed them from there.
Honorable Chairperson, the day is not far when Karnali will not only be a province with electricity access but a province with reliable, quality, and sustainable electricity service. For this, the Karnali Province Electrification Project is planned to be carried out in two phases. In the first phase, distribution lines will be extended and transformers installed in Salyan, Rukum Paschim, Jajarkot, Kalikot, Jumla, and Mugu. Bids have been invited for this. The second phase aims to ensure complete electrification in the entire Karnali Province by establishing 33 and 11 kV sub-stations and distribution systems in Upper Dolpa. We are clear that geographical difficulties and distance should not be reasons to deprive citizens of electricity access. Where the national transmission line is economically and technically feasible, the transmission system will be expanded. Where it is difficult to reach the national grid immediately, the government has prepared an action plan to ensure electricity access through micro-hydropower, solar mini-grids, and domestic solar systems. I also inform you that with the cooperation and coordination of the Government of Nepal, provinces, and local levels, the Nepal Electricity Authority and the Alternative Energy Promotion Center are committed to completing the electrification of Karnali within the stipulated time. I conclude my remarks here. Long live Nepal.
Honorable Chairperson: - Honorable members, now that the questioning Honorable Member wishes to ask a supplementary question, I will provide time to ask a supplementary question focusing on the subject.
Honorable Mr. Bishnu Bahadur Bishwakarma (Nepal Communist Party): - Honorable Chairperson, through the Honorable Chairperson, I want to ask the Minister: I am happy to hear that bids have been invited for transformer installation in some districts. May that work be completed within the stipulated time. Let the process of electrification of the remaining Upper Dolpa be expedited.
The condition of line extension in the electrified and partially electrified wards is dire. Poles have fallen, and in some places, poles are half-fallen. Low-voltage wires are scattered all over the roads, fields, and sometimes in the forests and hills. Due to these abandoned wires, in Kalikot alone, 2 people in Narharinath Rural Municipality, 2 people in Sannitriveni Rural Municipality, 9 people in Shubhakalika Rural Municipality, 1 person in Raskot Municipality, and 1 person in Tilagufa Municipality, a total of 7 people have lost their lives. When will the abandoned and scattered wires be managed, and when will the bidding for the electrification of Upper Dolpa be announced? I ask these questions. Thank you.
Honorable Chairperson: - Honorable Minister.
Honorable Minister of Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation, Biraj Bhakta Shrestha: - Thank you, Honorable Chairperson. It is very justified, Honorable Member. This happened. Initially, the challenge was to provide electricity, not necessarily quality electricity, just to light up. Now, regarding quality, like how many sub-stations should be there, at what distance, initially, it was just about the wires. This led to problems of voltage drop and tripping. Geographically, as the Honorable Chairperson might have seen in the assembly today, two major 132 kV lines in Karnali were destroyed by landslides, and questions were raised about their quality. In those areas, there are problems with poles during the time of wind and rain. This is a nationwide issue, not just in Nepal; during the rainy season, there are problems with short circuits in the electricity.

6. Regarding the query raised by the Honourable Member, the Authority has also taken a significant load this time. What has happened is that many of our employees have been injured and fallen ill due to this. Therefore, I also express my condolences to those who have lost their lives due to this reason. I also wish for the speedy recovery of the injured. Now, regarding those who go through the forest area, it seems that even a small gust of wind can cause damage to the entire transmission line due to falling tree branches. In the forest area, we are also preparing to leave a little more space on the sides of the right-of-way, where the transmission line passes. This is not just for this year; every year, in Ashar, Shrawan, and Bhadra, these issues, due to geographical and seasonal challenges, trouble us.

Regarding the issue of wires raised by the Honourable Member, we have told the Chief of the Press that this time, the response of the employees of the Authority has been very good, and I am proud of it. This time, when I myself went to Karnali, there was no crane of the Authority in the entire Karnali. So, this time we have handed over a crane from the Bagmati Province. There are geographical challenges, such as the need to work at great heights and having to travel through difficult terrain to identify faults, and challenges with resources, Honourable Member. However, our diligent employees of the Authority are working hard, braving the sun and rain, to the best of their ability. In this regard, I would like to request the Honourable Member that this time, a specific budget has been allocated to Karnali Province itself. The authority to set priorities and undertake necessary actions, with the active participation of you and other representatives, will also be transferred there. Regarding Dolpa, what we have done this time is that when the tender is delayed, it seems that the practice of working only towards the end of the fiscal year has become prevalent. This time, we have completed about 60 percent of the tenders under our ministry. I will inquire about the status of Dolpa, or the Honourable Member can also inquire with the relevant body about the reasons for the delay, whether there are any technical reasons. I request this. Thank you.
